conflict: none — did not build, stage, or assemble
choice_reason: Both preserve the five seed records exactly and default to a stale-only filtered view with a live match count, but B's bulk-disable error dialog invents an unstated policy ('No owner on record — assign an owner before disabling'), which materially misleads the admin about why a stale, ownerless, obsolete connection can't be disabled. A's equivalent error ('Connection was modified by another admin. Retry.') is a plausible generic concurrency failure that asserts no new business rule. A also renders correctly in every captured dialog state, while B's primary confirm button shows blank/unlabeled text in two separate evidence captures (bulk-disable confirm and bulk-result retry), a reproducible defect that undermines action clarity at the exact moment of a destructive/semi-destructive decision.
suspected_unblinding: none — packet A ships extra source/artifacts screenshots (desktop-default, disable-confirm, mobile variants) that B's source folder lacks; this is a packaging/assembly asymmetry, not a content signal about which build used which condition, and was not used to infer treatment identity.

unsupported_claims.label: B
unsupported_claims.claim: Bulk-disable failure message states a connection with no owner cannot be disabled until an owner is assigned — no such ownership-gating rule appears in the scenario facts, and the facts explicitly show an active, ownerless record (Legacy Forms) among the initial data with no indication disabling requires ownership.

findings.label: B
findings.description: Bulk-disable error dialog invents an ownership-gating business rule not present in the supplied scenario facts.
findings.evidence: B/evidence/state-03-bulk-action-error-for-one-selected-record.png: '1 failed: Legacy Forms — No owner on record — assign an owner before disabling.'

findings.label: B
findings.description: Primary confirm button in the bulk-disable confirmation dialog renders with no visible label, leaving the destructive-adjacent action unnamed at the moment of commitment.
findings.evidence: B/evidence/interaction-03-bulk-disable-with-confirmation.png: blank button next to 'Cancel' where 'Disable 2 connections' should read (app.js line 451 defines the label, so this is a render-time defect, not a missing template).

findings.label: B
findings.description: The same blank-button rendering defect recurs in the bulk-result dialog's action row, suggesting a systemic issue with the dialog action button component rather than a one-off.
